domain.value: video tokenizer family (3D/2D conv autoencoder with AlphaBlender temporal sampling; KL or FSQ regularizer) for video generation / world models; trained on a self-collected set of natural videos

quotes.quote: VidTok is a cutting-edge family of video tokenizers that delivers state-of-the-art performance in both continuous and discrete tokenizations with various compression rates.
* Video generation on the continuous / discrete latent tokens.
1. Training Set 1 consists of approximately 400K of low-resolution videos (e.g., 480p). The videos are natural videos with diverse lightning, motions, and scenarios.

architecture.type: convolutional video autoencoder: separate spatial (2D) and temporal (AlphaBlender + 1D/3D conv) down/up-sampling; causal or non-causal; KL (continuous) or FSQ (discrete) bottleneck
architecture.representation: encoder latents: C channels (4/8/16 for KL; FSQ codes for discrete) on a (1+(T-1)/4) x H/8 x W/8 grid for 4x8x8 causal variants

pretraining_data.summary: Self-collected natural-video dataset in two subsets: model card says Training Set 1 ~400K low-res (480p) videos and Training Set 2 ~10K high-res (1080p) videos; the paper says ~10 million and ~6 million videos respectively (inconsistent counts between card and paper, recorded as found). No dataset or provider named. Evaluation on MCL-JCV and a web-video validation set (WebVid-Val) only.

quotes.quote: For training, we utilize a self-collected video dataset, divided into two subsets based on video quality: (1) Training Set 1, comprising approximately 10 10 million low-resolution videos (e.g., 480p); and (2) Training Set 2, consisting of approximately 6 6 million high-resolution videos (e.g., 1080p). All videos in the dataset are natural videos characterized by diverse lighting conditions, motion patterns, and scenarios.
